fields.acceptance: A testscript in a git repo commits with Change: <id> and Actor: builder, then writes Evidence verifying the change set's leaf: as builder, check --json exits 0 with one warn finding on rule evidence-actor naming the four; as verifier, no such finding; a commit with no Actor: trailer yields none. Go tests run the rule on given commit trailers, so check itself still runs no git.
fields.statement: rhiza check warns, on a rule named evidence-actor, for each live Evidence that verifies a capability when the Evidence's actor is named in an Actor: trailer of a commit carrying the Change: trailer of the change set that added that capability, unless the commit's Leaf: trailers name other leaves only. The warning names the Evidence, the capability, the actor and the commit. Outside a git work tree the rule is skipped, silently.

A commit's Leaf: trailers scope the evidence-actor warning: a commit with Leaf: trailers counts only for the leaves they name, by handle or ID; a commit with a Change: trailer and no Leaf: counts for every capability of its change set.
fields.wording: the planning agent's proposal, accepted by the owner

fields.statement: Outside a git work tree the evidence-actor rule is skipped with no finding, since append-only already warns that git is missing.
fields.wording: the planning agent's proposal, accepted by the owner

fields.statement: evidence-actor warns once per Evidence and capability, naming the oldest matching commit, and matches an Actor: trailer by the actor's handle or ID.

fields.statement: A leaf's needs in change show lists every live capability it depends on, in or out of the change set; build order is worked out among the change set's own leaves, ties in tree order.
fields.wording: the planning agent's proposal, accepted by the owner

fields.statement: An Evidence node's actor is the actor stamped on the ops entry that first wrote its create; later writes by other actors, and replacing the create, do not change it.

fields.statement: A depends-on loop among capabilities is refused at write time naming the shortest path back, and reported by rhiza check on the depends-on rule, once per loop, naming its capabilities.
